mainEntity.name: How much does a BMW 2 Series 218d engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A BMW 2 Series 218d engine replacement typically costs between £1,699 and £3,300 depending on the condition (used, reconditioned, or rebuilt) and the specific engine code. Used engines start from around £1,100, reconditioned units from £1,699, and fully rebuilt engines with a 12-month warranty from £2,200. Labour for supply and fit adds approximately £800-£1,500 depending on the workshop.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain failure in a BMW 2 Series 218d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common early warning sign is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start, which typically disappears as the engine warms up. This affects N47-powered 218d models (2014-2015). Other symptoms include a metallic ticking sound, engine hesitation, and in severe cases, the engine management light illuminating with camshaft position errors.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a BMW 2 Series 218d?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the vehicle's value and the extent of the damage. For an N47-powered 218d (2014-2015) worth £5,000-£8,000, a reconditioned engine at £1,699-£2,100 is often worthwhile if you plan to keep the car. For B47 models (2015+) worth £8,000-£15,000, replacement is almost always justified. If the car is worth under £5,000, a used engine or repair may be more cost-effective.

mainEntity.name: How long does a BMW 2 Series 218d engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A typical BMW 2 Series 218d engine replacement takes 3-5 working days from order to completion, assuming the engine is in stock. Supply-only orders are usually dispatched within 1-2 working days. Supply and fit through our specialist network typically takes 3-5 days, including delivery, fitting, and ECU calibration. N47 timing chain replacement alone requires 12-18 hours of labour due to the rear-mounted chain.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the N47 and B47 engine in the 218d?

acceptedAnswer.text: The BMW 218d used the N47 engine from 2014-2015 (141hp) and the B47 from 2015 onwards (150hp). The B47 was introduced to address the N47's timing chain issues and improve emissions compliance. The B47 is generally more reliable, though it has its own EGR cooler problems. Both are 2.0-litre four-cylinder turbo diesels.

mainEntity.name: Will a replacement BMW 2 Series 218d engine pass the MoT?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes - all engines supplied through EnginesMarket are MoT emissions compliant. Rebuilt and reconditioned engines are tested to ensure they meet the original emissions standards for the vehicle's year. For diesel 218d models, this includes DPF and EGR system validation to ensure compliance with UK emissions regulations.

historyTimeline.h2: BMW 2 Series 218d - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The BMW 2 Series 218d arrived in 2014 as the entry-level diesel variant across the 2 Series range, powered initially by the N47 2.0-litre four-cylinder diesel engine. In 2015, the N47 was replaced by the revised B47 engine, bringing improved reliability, better emissions compliance, and a modest power increase.

milestones.description: N47D20C, 2.0L turbo diesel, 141hp (F22 Coupe, F23 Convertible, F45 Active Tourer launch)
B47D20A, 2.0L turbo diesel, 150hp (B47 introduced, replacing N47 across the range)
B47C20A, 2.0L transverse turbo diesel, 150hp (F45 Active Tourer, F46 Gran Tourer transverse mounting)
B47C20B, 2.0L transverse turbo diesel, 150hp (F45/F46 LCI update, emissions refinement)
B47D20A, 2.0L turbo diesel, 150hp (G42 218d Coupe, new generation with mild updates)

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the BMW 2 Series 218d is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: BMW 2 Series 218d Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: H3 (intro, 2-3 sentences): The BMW 2 Series 218d has been powered by two generations of 2.0-litre diesel engines: the earlier N47 (2014-2015) and the later B47 (2015-present). The N47 is notorious for timing chain failure, while the B47 suffers primarily from EGR cooler cracking and turbocharger issues. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure point, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why the BMW 2 Series 218d N47 Engine Fails Catastrophically
problems.rootCause: The N47 timing chain is located at the rear of the engine, making it inaccessible without removing the engine. The chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing the chain to stretch or snap. When the chain breaks, pistons strike valves, causing bent valves, damaged rocker arms, and often a written-off engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove engine, replace chain, tensioner, guides
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early (rattling noise only)

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded timing components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: The right call if engine has suffered internal damage

problems.recommendation: If you own an N47-powered 218d and hear a rattling noise on cold start, have the timing chain inspected immediately - preventative replacement is significantly cheaper than a full rebuild after failure. If the chain has already snapped, a rebuilt engine with upgraded components and a 12-month warranty is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt N47D20C BMW 2 Series 218d engine prices

problems.h4: EGR Cooler Cracking - BMW 2 Series 218d B47 Diesel Coolant Loss
problems.rootCause: The EGR cooler on B47 engines can develop cracks, leading to coolant loss and potential overheating. In some cases, coolant mixing with exhaust gases can cause DPF blockages and further emissions system damage.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cracked EGR cooler with upgraded unit
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before DPF damage

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace cooler, clean or replace DPF
repairOptions.longevity: Required if DPF is blocked by coolant contamination

repairOptions.specialistPrice: £2,400-£3,300 (matches Section 4's rebuilt figure for B47 codes)
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, upgraded EGR components, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: If overheating has caused head gasket or piston damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - for a typical £8,000-£15,000 B47 218d, EGR cooler replacement is a worthwhile repair. Only consider full engine replacement if overheating has caused secondary internal damage.
problems.recommendation: EGR cooler failure on the B47 is a known issue. Replace the cooler promptly if you notice coolant loss or a sweet smell from the exhaust. Upgraded metal-core EGR coolers are available and should be specified in any replacement to prevent recurrence.
problems.cta: -> Get quotes for B47 BMW 2 Series 218d engine replacement

problems.h4: Turbocharger Wastegate Rattle - BMW 2 Series 218d Boost Pressure Loss
problems.affectedModels: BMW 2 Series 218d (B47 and N47 variants, all years)
problems.rootCause: The turbocharger wastegate actuator can develop play, causing a rattling noise and loss of boost pressure. This is particularly noticeable under acceleration and can trigger the engine management light.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if turbo core is undamaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Strip, clean, rebuild turbo with new actuator
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended if turbo has shaft play or oil leaks

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit, includes updated turbo components
repairOptions.longevity: If turbo failure has caused engine damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: As above - turbo repair is usually worthwhile on all 218d variants given the vehicle's value. Full engine replacement is rarely needed for turbo failure alone.
problems.recommendation: Wastegate rattle is common on higher-mileage 218d diesel engines. Replace the actuator early to prevent further turbo wear. If the turbo has already failed, a reconditioned or rebuilt engine with upgraded components may be the most cost-effective solution.
